vocabulary.planned: Not started; no merged implementation on main.
vocabulary.in_progress: Started or partially satisfied; see status_evidence for what exists and what remains.
vocabulary.completed: Implemented and merged with CI green; a named acceptance aspect still needs validation (see status_evidence).
vocabulary.verified: Implemented, merged, CI green, with dedicated automated test coverage on main (see status_evidence).

product_mandate: open-source, local-first with optional secure remote access; macOS-first; hardware-independent, model-independent and provider-independent. Users can install or select future lightweight models without rebuilding the application, subject to runtime and capability compatibility.
non_negotiable_principles: No orchestration code assumes a particular chip, memory tier, model ID or vendor SDK.
All model/provider adapters expose negotiated capabilities, normalized errors, streaming and tool-call semantics.
Users can explicitly pin a model/provider per task, switch when compatible, and revert; no unapproved cloud transmission or spending.
New model releases are discovered and verified by immutable model ID/digest, version, quantization and runtime compatibility.
Benchmark-driven recommendations consider measured quality, latency, TTFT, prefill/decode throughput, peak memory, cost, privacy and confidence.
Execution is policy-controlled, auditable, resumable and isolated; hybrid remote access is opt-in and private-network-first.
Never claim that switching models preserves identical answers, tool behavior or context capacity; negotiate and warn instead.

architecture.component_boundary_overview: Web UI / CLI -> typed FastAPI application -> workflow engine + tool policy -> capability router + resource scheduler -> provider adapters (MLX/oMLX, Ollama, llama.cpp, cloud APIs) -> hardware/runtime adapters.
architecture.shared_services: Shared services: model registry, benchmark profiles, context engine, MCP, SQLite migrations, traces, audit and approvals.
architecture.core_contracts: ModelDescriptor: immutable model identity/digest, source, revision, quantization, runtime, capabilities, context limit, tool/schema/stream support, trust/provenance. HardwareProfile: OS, architecture, accelerators, physical and available memory, pressure, installed runtimes and permissions. RoutingDecision: feasible candidates, policy exclusions, selected model, fallback reasons, user consent and estimated budget.

implementation_playbook.session_start_prompt: You are a senior engineer working on Adaptive Runtime, an open-source, local-first and optionally secure-remote AI developer platform. It must be hardware-independent, LLM-independent and provider-independent. macOS is the initial supported platform; avoid chip/RAM/model/vendor hardcoding. Preserve local-only privacy and never trigger cloud requests, billable use or destructive tools without explicit user authorization. Before coding: inspect the current repository and pinned commit; identify relevant modules, tests, API and DB contracts, open ADRs, and actual existing behavior. Do not assume the roadmap matches the code. Summarize current state, gaps, dependencies, risks and a minimal implementation plan. Ask only if a blocking ambiguity exists. Work on exactly one story per session. Implement the smallest maintainable change, with typed contracts, backward compatibility or migration, negative tests, security boundaries, observability and docs. Do not introduce new dependencies or change public APIs silently. Run relevant checks, report commands/results, failures, changed files and acceptance-criterion evidence. Do not claim tests were run if they were not. Never commit/push or access external services unless authorized. At the end provide: (1) implementation summary; (2) acceptance checklist with evidence; (3) test results; (4) security/privacy assessment; (5) migration/rollback considerations; (6) remaining risks and next dependent story.
implementation_playbook.story_prompt_template: Implement [STORY_ID]: [STORY_TITLE]. Priority: [P0/P1/P2]. Dependencies: [DEPENDENCIES]. Acceptance criteria: [ACCEPTANCE]. First inspect existing code and show whether dependencies are implemented and verified. Identify exact files and interfaces; propose the smallest safe change. Implement with tests (positive, negative, failure/recovery as applicable), documentation, and evidence for each acceptance criterion. Do not implement unrelated stories. If blocked, stop and report the blocker and required prerequisite. Return a concise PR-ready summary.

model_benchmarking_safeguards: Calibration inputs: model digest/revision, quantization, runtime version, hardware profile, prompt tokens, output tokens, concurrency, temperature and context length.
Measure TTFT, prompt/prefill throughput, decode throughput, peak memory, warm vs cold startup, failure rate and task-quality score separately.
Report medians and spread across multiple runs; compare only compatible tasks and disclose differences in measurement environment.
Recommendation policy: hard-filter by tool/schema/context/privacy/resource compatibility, then rank by user-selected priorities (quality, latency, cost, energy if measurable).
Community data is advisory: validate schema, signatures/provenance where available, license, and mark imported data as unverified until reproduced.
first_execution_sequence: Sprint 1: AS-001, AS-002, AS-003, AS-006 and AS-005. Sprint 2: AS-007, AS-008, AS-015, AS-017 and AS-051. Then build admission control (AS-018), consent-aware routing (AS-021/058), switching (AS-052/054/055), and calibration (AS-059/060) before UI recommendation (AS-061/062). Run security and recovery tracks in parallel once their core dependencies are ready.
